cycle_title: One-shot end-to-end central theorem draft (PI request)
completed: Drafted docs/central_theorem_full_draft.md: a single chain from omitted context to the response law, KL separation, and BIC, Bayes-factor and exact trial-LOO selection, with boundary results and a gap ledger.

New in this draft: exact within-person dependence signature (every homogeneous model is false); second-order heterogeneity expansion splitting omission into attenuation and dependence directions; extra-score drift criterion with a rigorous gap lower bound and a score-test approximation; weighted-least-squares mechanism criterion with Delta_C = Delta_J / T for homogeneous candidates; hierarchical absorption (order eps^6 or eps^8) and a parity obstruction for context-dependent dispersion.
Added scripts/verify_central_theorem_draft.py (dependency-free) and its output logs/theory_checks/2026-10-02_central_theorem_draft.json; all checks pass.
why_it_matters: Shows the full logical flow the PI asked for and separates what is proved (homogeneous candidates, finite designs, fixed T) from what is conditional (hierarchical candidates) or open.
The drift approximation Delta_J ~ Lambda^2 / (2 I) reproduces the witness gap to 0.3 percent from the simple fit alone, and Laplace/TIC heuristics explain the pilot's BF/LOO-versus-BIC ordering.

risks_or_uncertainties: New results (Thm 1.4, Thm 2.4, Prop 2.5, Cor 2.7, Props 4.3-4.4) are author-checked only.
Hierarchical-candidate version of the theorem remains conditional on H1-H2, a nonzero drift at the hierarchical projection and L > 0.
Analysis suggests the research-spec target of misselection as task length grows may fail for hierarchical candidates under trial LOO (open problem O3).
Background references in Appendix B are not yet verified against source.
